newsitem.title: USA: Abortion foes fall short in Senate recall drive.
newsitem.headline: Abortion foes fall short in Senate recall drive.

text.p: Abortion foes on Tuesday failed to collect enough petition signatures to force a recall vote on Wisconsin's two Democratic U.S. senators.

A Milwaukee-based organization called First Breath Alliance presented the petitions, collected over a 60-day period, at state election headquarters in Madison but announced it had fallen several thousand signatures short.
The group said it had 349,948 signatures to recall Sen. Russ Feingold and 343,494 against Sen. Herb Kohl. A total of 391,000 signatures were required against each senator to force a recall.

"Obviously there was a groundswell of support," said alliance founder Norbert Nicholas, a Cedarburg, Wisconsin, insurance executive. "We believe we have made a sea change in what Wisconsin politics looks like."

The senators were targeted because of their opposition to federal legislation banning so-called "partial birth" abortions. Both houses of Congress passed the ban, but it did not get enough Senate votes to override an expected veto from President Clinton.
Nicholas said his group had not ruled out another recall effort but would more likely use the names collected to mount regular election campaigns against the two men.
Kohl, 62, is in his second term. Feingold, 44, is serving his first.

If the drives had been successful the two senators would have been forced to run for re-election before their terms were up. But the state Democratic party had already announced plans to go to court had the petitions been filed.

Opponents of the effort had branded it illegal. The U.S. Constitution does not address the issue directly, legal experts said, but courts have held states cannot set regulations for electing members of Congress.
Leaders of the effort, however, said the 10th Amendment -- the one that reserves to the states powers not delegated to the federal government -- gave them a legal foothold.
